title: Reduce transcript persistence work exposed by SQLite overflow-record comparisons
outcome: Dump termal (2).DMP, captured 2026-09-07 19:06 PDT, shows thread 27 / 0xbb6c termal-persist allocating 385312 bytes inside SQLite 3.46.0 sqlite3BtreeIndexMoveto, reached from OP_NoConflict during INSERT INTO messages. Bound row: session-5703, position 43, message-555114, JSON 1055 bytes. Comparison record: session-5705, position 4, message-555327, git diff output, full record 385293 bytes. The messages table is WITHOUT ROWID, so this PK lookup encounters full message payloads and takes the overflow-record allocation/read path. src/persist.rs:3132 also deletes the retained transcript tail and reinserts every retained message for each changed session. Persistence thread accrued 108m24.608s CPU of 156m02s process CPU over 7h34m16s uptime. Single-snapshot evidence proves the current operation, not its historical frequency or share of CPU. Investigate both per-message persistence deltas and a rowid-backed or separated-body schema, preserving transcript order, updates, truncation, deletion and atomicity. Benchmark representative synthetic/offline fixtures before selecting a fix; do not open the live database. Evidence: target/dump-analysis-20260907/analysis.md and associated CDB logs.
disposal_reason: Backlog triage w-930e4d333f07 (Architect1 batch 1 re-check with marker, spot-checked by Termal::Fable2): CLOSE-DONE.
